title: KL divergence on a finite space as a log-likelihood-ratio sum
statement:
Let $\Omega$ be a finite discrete measurable space, and let $\mu$ and $
u$ be finite measures on $\Omega$. If there is a point $\omega \in \Omega$ with $
u(\{\omega\}) = 0$ but $\mu(\{\omega\}) 
eq 0$, then the Kullback–Leibler divergence is infinite, $D_{\mathrm{KL}}(\mu \,\|\, 
u) = \infty$. Otherwise,
\[
  D_{\mathrm{KL}}(\mu \,\|\, 
u)
  = \left(\ \sum_{\omega \in \Omega} \mu(\{\omega\})\,\log rac{d\mu}{d
u}(\omega)\ +\ 
u(\Omega)\ -\ \mu(\Omega)\ ight)_{\!+},
\]
where $\log rac{d\mu}{d
u}$ denotes the log-likelihood ratio of $\mu$ with respect to $
u$, the measures are read as their real values, and $(x)_+$ takes the enclosed real number as a nonnegative extended real, sending any negative value to $0$.
